sentences: Settle in.
You're starting in Midtown.
When you're ready, head for Bryant Park — about a 14-minute walk from here.
Look out at the green expanse ahead, with its twirling carousel and clustered little eateries.
Take a moment to take it in.
See the fountain? It's where Diane Keaton, playing an amateur sleuth, quizzes her husband about their supposedly bloodthirsty elderly neighbor.
That's a scene from Manhattan Murder Mystery, made in 1993.
Woody Allen directed it, and true to form he filled it with New York locales — the National Arts Club, over in Gramercy Park, among them.
Here's the twist: this leafy oasis was a crime-ridden hellscape in the '70s, the kind of place people called 'Needle Park'.
Long before that, back in 1853, this same lawn hosted the Crystal Palace Fair.
Today it's a four-acre lawn behind the beaux-arts New York Public Library, ringed with benches and London planetrees.
New Yorkers liken it to the Tuileries in Paris, a green break from the crush of high-rises.
Grab a coffee at a kiosk and the day fills up around you: free juggling at noon, yoga, painting, even birding tours.
From May through October the Sixth Avenue end turns into a stage for Broadway performers and free open-air movies on Monday nights.
Over on the east edge sits one of the city's most popular outdoor bars.
Come winter, the middle of the park becomes The Pond, a free ice rink circled by a European-style holiday market and its hot-chocolate booths.
Skating there is free, and lessons are on offer if you've never laced up.
For years this was home to New York Fashion Week, twice a year, until it moved to Lincoln Center in 2010.
That's Bryant Park — a onetime Needle Park that grew a carousel.
From here, make your way to your final destination.
That's the walk — you've reached your finish point.
